Primary request: Repose the exact frozen Image 2 Nyra and exact frozen Image 2 storm-shear weapon into ONE physically extreme, violently arrested full-body keyframe. This is the instant the moving blade mass is caught at maximum upper-right extension and pulls the entire body off-axis. Change only pose, anatomical loading, and physically consistent equipment response. Do not redesign costume, face, hair, yoke, circuit, capacitor, greaves, palette, weapon, guard, cage, hilt, or pommel.

Pose contract: massive character-RIGHT foot planted forward/down-right with its huge broad sole fully compressed into ground; right ankle deeply closed, right knee deeply flexed and tracking over that sole, right hip dropped directly into the same compressed load column. Character-LEFT foot far rear on forefoot only, heel conspicuously high, toes gripping and dragged inward toward the load column; no flat rear heel and no equal two-foot support. Pelvis rotates hard opposite ribcage. Spine visibly forms a loaded C-curve and side-bends away from the moving blade. Ribcage pitches off-axis, never upright. Head counter-turns toward viewer-left threat while eyes remain alert.

Upper-body chain: character-right scapula protracts and drives down/forward; character-left scapula retracts and separates visibly, creating unmistakable push-pull across shoulders. Right elbow is tightly compressed; left elbow reaches longer and more extended. Both wrists stay straight and loaded. Both complete hands visibly enclose separated regions of the SAME continuous cobalt hilt: leading right hand immediately behind the guard, trailing left hand near pommel, visible exposed wrap and ivory separator between them, exact plausible digits, pressure shadows, no hover or fusion.

Weapon physics: exactly ONE complete frozen Round010 broad-backed blackened-steel storm-shear, not an odachi and not redesigned. Its center of mass lies well outside the torso toward upper-right. One decisive steep diagonal axis from lower-left pommel through both hands and guard to upper-right clipped blade tip; never horizontal at waist. Full pommel, hilt, guard, base cage, broad blade, and tip visible with margin. Blade mass visibly drags wrists, elbows, scapulae, ribs and shoulder line toward upper-right while pelvis and right greave arrest it down-right.

Reactive equipment: every secondary element reacts opposite the arrest direction with one coherent timing. Short braid, cobalt cloth tails, straps, yoke mount, right-hip capacitor belt, ivory ceramic plates, and protected copper conductor all trail, tension, compress, buckle slightly, or shear consistently toward upper-left/left relative to the blade's caught upper-right travel; no random wind. Right-side plates and capacitor belt dig into the compressed hip; left-side straps stretch; yoke remains firmly attached and mount visibly taut; copper route remains continuous and protected.

Style/medium: premium original 2D industrial-mythic fantasy concept painting matching Image 2, controlled hand-painted edges, matte worn cobalt/ivory/blackened-steel/oxidized-copper material separation, restrained natural studio light.

Composition/framing: native 1536x1024 landscape. Exactly one complete adult woman and one complete weapon. Full head, braid, attached yoke, both arms/hands, both legs/feet, raised rear heel and toes, planted right sole, pommel, guard/cage, entire blade and tip all fully inside generous margins. Pale neutral warm-gray studio ground; one small physical right-foot contact shadow and a subtle short rear-toe skid/gouge are allowed.

Final-art prohibitions: NO force arrow, diagram mark, joint circle, text, label, logo, watermark, environment, enemy, architecture, lightning, glow, particles, sparks, speed lines, action smear, motion blur, dust cloud, or crop.

Hard reject: static wide greatsword hold; bilateral balance; flat rear heel; upright quiet torso; quiet scapulae; hilt across waist; blade mass not driving body; hand hover; malformed digits; duplicate or detached weapon; body penetration; identity/design drift; bare-arm or fetish amplification; extra person; cropped foot, yoke, pommel, guard, cage, or blade tip.

exact_prompt_lines: Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: final bounded targeted Ground-Arc Arrest kinetic correction, P10 Round011 candidate 04 of 04

Inputs: Image 1 is the immediate art base. Preserve its exact Nyra face, short asymmetric braid, attached left ivory yoke, protected continuous copper route, right-hip capacitor, heavy right grounding greave/lighter left leg, cobalt/ivory/blackened-steel/copper materials, exact one-piece non-historical storm-shear, one-person framing, and valid two-hand same-hilt contact. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL joint/load guide and must control the corrected silhouette; never render its arrow, labels, circles, or lines. Image 3 freezes Round010 art/design. Image 4 freezes Round007 identity.
Change ONLY four kinetic facts; do not redesign or add anything.

1. REAR FOOT TOPOLOGY: lift the character-LEFT heel dramatically until there is a clearly visible boot-height wedge of pale empty background beneath the heel and rear half of the sole. Only the ball and toe cap touch the floor at far lower-left. Plantar-flex the ankle steeply; drag toes inward/down-right and show a tiny short toe gouge. The rear heel cannot touch its shadow and cannot share load.

2. HILT LIFT: move the entire connected pommel+hilt+both already-gripping hands+guard+blade rigidly together upward and clockwise. Pommel at about x=585,y=600; trailing left hand x=675,y=530; leading right hand x=805,y=425; guard x=875,y=350; blade tip x=1440,y=65. The continuous hilt must cross diagonally in front of lower chest, not horizontally at waist or pelvis. Keep both hands closed on separated cobalt regions of the same hilt, separator visible, wrists straight, exact plausible digits.

3. PUSH-PULL CHAIN: visibly dislocate the comfortable symmetry without injury. Character-right scapula and shoulder drive far forward/down toward the guard; right elbow folds tightly under the leading fist near the ribs. Character-left scapula retracts far back/up; left shoulder opens and left elbow reaches much longer behind/left before the forearm returns to trailing hand. Shoulder line is steeply tilted; one elbow sharply compressed, the other substantially extended. Bow the spine more deeply into a C away from the blade and rotate ribcage hard against the dropped pelvis. Sternum pitches diagonally; head counter-turns viewer-left. The blade mass must appear to pull the whole upper chain upper-right.

4. EQUIPMENT LAG: all loose/reactive elements share one opposite direction, upper-left/left: braid lifts and streams left; cobalt cloth tails and straps lift left rather than hang vertically; attached yoke mount stretches taut; right-hip capacitor belt digs into compressed hip; ceramic plates gap on the extended left side and compress on the right; copper conductor stays continuous but tensions visibly. No random wind and no motion blur.

Right load column remains massive and singular: right foot planted forward/down-right, broad sole flattened, ankle deeply closed, knee flexed over sole, hip dropped above it. Full person, both feet, attached yoke, pommel, guard/cage, complete broad blade and tip all inside 1536x1024 landscape with margin. Pale neutral warm-gray studio ground, contact shadows and tiny toe gouge only.

Final art contains NO guide arrow/marks/text, no label/logo/watermark, no environment/enemy, no lightning/glow/particles/sparks/speed lines/blur/dust cloud, no extra person, no duplicate/detached weapon, no body penetration, no crop, no bare/fetish amplification.

Hard reject if rear heel is flat or low, hilt remains at waist, shoulders/elbows are bilateral, torso is upright/quiet, equipment hangs neutrally, any hand hovers or is malformed, or identity/design changes.

decision.finding: Candidate 04 materially improves the isolated Ground-Arc Arrest contract over candidates 01–03: chest-height diagonal hilt, upper-right external blade mass, dominant compressed right load column, airborne rear heel with toe skid, pelvis/ribcage opposition, and coherent leftward secondary lag. Promotion is evidence for fresh criticism only. It does not establish a complete design-freeze pass because braid identity drifts to two tails, scapular opposition is moderate, the C-curve is not deeply compressed, and blade/front-boot forms are exaggerated.
